A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KeyDiff research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, including the rotated result tables. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench and needle-in-a-haystack evaluations, ablations, and empirical analyses of key/query geometry.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds Math-500, Phonebook Lookup, correlation analysis, and GPU/mobile timing experiments.

M1.justification: The key-similarity scoring, mean-anchor approximation and blockwise eviction procedure are retained. The sliding-window variant highlighted in v4 Section 3.2 already appears as KeyDiff + Recent tokens with 10% and 20% reservations in v1 Table 11, retained as v4 Table 14.

E1.justification: v4 adds mathematical reasoning on Math-500, involving short prompts and long generations, and Phonebook Lookup for name-to-number retrieval. Existing LongBench coverage and needle-in-a-haystack tests remain. The RULER discussion explicitly references community-produced results rather than documenting an original RULER experiment.

E2.justification: v4 adds SnapKV to the needle-in-a-haystack comparison and introduces a full-cache reference for its recall-difference analysis. Sink results move to Figure 19. The LongBench comparator set is unchanged: KeyL2Norm already appears in v1 Table 8, although v4 adds its citation.

E3.justification: Existing LongBench settings are retained. New protocols include sampled Math-500 generation with a 20% recent-token window, FlexMatch/ExactMatch evaluation, GPU TTFT comparisons using eager and FlashAttention, and FP16 Android scoring measurements. Math-500 generation limits are inconsistently documented: Appendix E lists 6144, while the corresponding tables specify 8K.

E4.justification: v4 adds quantitative geometry-attention correlation analysis, additional key/query PCA views, and broader layer/head diagnostics. Math-500 Tables 5 and 7 examine subsets where eviction is actually triggered, while Table 18 analyzes recall differences against full caching. The original anchor, distance-metric, block-size and recent-token analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 reports averaging five sampled Math-500 responses and five random phonebooks, adds shaded timing variability, and reports a mean and standard deviation for correlations. These reporting practices were absent from v1. Timing-band definitions, timing repetition counts and formal significance tests remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Matched LongBench and ablation values remain unchanged, but substantial new reasoning, retrieval, correlation and latency results appear. For example, v4 Table 4 reports Math-500 FlexMatch of 0.844 for KeyDiff and 0.828 for SnapKV with 4K caches and an 8K generation cap, versus 0.840 with full caching. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: The optimization relaxation and geometric proofs already present in v1 are retained and reorganized. v4 states a large-n form of the attention-weight bound and revises operation-cost assumptions, changing the derived cost from (6d+18)n+d+17 to (12d+97)n+3d+94. The linear-complexity conclusion remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The attention-free eviction and LongBench claims remain, but v4 substantially broadens its headline contributions. Its abstract and introduction newly claim near-full-cache Math-500 performance for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and up to 30% lower end-to-end inference latency.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to GQA-based models and identifies MLA integration as future work. Appendix E newly hypothesizes that stronger KV compression makes Qwen more sensitive to eviction than Llama. The original attention-sink and key/query geometry explanations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds A100 80GB hardware information, Transformers v4.49/BFloat16/11K-prompt details for the eager TTFT experiment, reasoning sampling parameters, and FP16 Android timing information. Its checklist explicitly discloses that the code is proprietary and unreleased; v1 had no corresponding availability statement. The exact smartphone remains unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds focused references for Longformer, the L2-norm eviction baseline, DeepSeek-R1, MATH and Qwen, plus brief positioning against community RULER results. The related-work organization and distinctions among sparse attention, cache compression and token eviction remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, and the theoretical narrative is reorganized: geometric results enter Section 3.3 while the optimization derivation moves to Appendix C.2. Detailed ablations move to Appendix G, the supplementary sections are reorganized, and a NeurIPS checklist is added.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two columns to a single-column layout. v4 adds key/query PCA and latency figures, replaces selected geometry histograms/bar charts with layer/head heatmaps, and adds reasoning, correlation, retrieval and mobile-timing tables. Existing displays, including Sink retrieval results and ablation tables, are relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens support for the method through quantitative correlation analysis, generation-heavy reasoning evaluation, and measured GPU/mobile efficiency, addressing gaps in v1's evidence. These gains are tempered by inconsistent Math-500 settings, undefined timing uncertainty bands, and an end-to-end latency claim supported by TTFT and scoring measurements rather than full-response timing. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
